notes.title: Updated to 1.92
notes.content:
[b]The next Celtreos patch is live![/b]

[h1]New Setting “No Negative Items”[/h1]
This new setting prevents [b]all[/b] negative items from spawning in the game, which tends to make the game significantly easier to play.  (This includes all red-orb items like slow-down, destroy-weapon, reduce-range, reduce-power, zero-score, etc.)

[h1]Artwork Improvements[/h1]
More artwork tweaks have been made, mostly noticeable on the title screen and in the first stage, “Colony Evacuation”.

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
A stage-related trophy was accidentally awarded by starting [i]any[/i] game.  While this trophy will not be deleted as part of the fix, for new owners of the game it will now trigger under the correct conditions.

Also, while not strictly a bug, it could be confusing if external audio (such as Apple Music) was preventing music selections during the game so new explanatory text appears when game music is disabled.

notes.title: Updated to 1.90
notes.content:
[b]A big update to Celtreos![/b]

[h1]New “Lateral” Weapon[/h1]
A 5th sideways-class weapon, “Lateral”, has been added to the Plasma Series (and can be used in custom weapon arrays).  This fires modules above and below your ship that damage anything they touch, while also periodically firing forward or backward from the current locations of the modules.

Furthermore, this weapon has 5 variations because it fires your default-class weapon (Beam, Gun, Laser, Ring or Rocket)!  Some variants, like Beam, can produce substantially different covering fire.

[h1]New XP×4 Item[/h1]
Similar to existing XP×2 but this item [i]quadruples[/i] accumulated experience points for the current weapon.  It does not last long!

[h1]Minor Gameplay Updates[/h1]
Power-ups now “stack” on the left side to an extent, if you pick up several of them at once.

The Razor weapon has been slightly modified to have a tighter firing range.

A problem with the physics of the Bumper has been fixed, that made the ship [i]more[/i] vulnerable to regular fire (even though it was much less vulnerable to walls).

The UI has been tweaked so that buttons bound to the Return key have a slightly different style.

[h1]Soundtrack Improvement[/h1]
Minor changes to the “Mystery” song (used in the “Dark Nebula” stage).

notes.title: Updated to 1.85
notes.content:
[b]The next Celtreos patch is live![/b]

[h1]New EXP Tiers[/h1]
Each weapon slot now has 5 Tiers instead of 4, with a new set of updates possible for each slot!  Look for the following:
[list]
[*] [b]Enlarge[/b] (destroyer weapons): Always fire larger projectiles
[*] [b]Expand[/b] (default and sideways weapons): Cover a larger area
[*] [b]Power Up[/b] (opposer weapons): Do more damage
[*] [b]Range Up[/b] (locator weapons): Detect enemies from further away
[*] [b]Resilience[/b] (default weapons): Prevent reduction below a power level of 3
[*] [b]Waves[/b] (multiway weapons): Periodically fire larger projectiles
[/list]
[h1]New EXP UI[/h1]
There is now a bar underneath the main Tier display that shows more granular EXP acquisition, split into two parts.  The first part is static, aligned with any obtained Tiers, showing EXP that has already resulted in awards.  The flashing range shows “pending” EXP that will turn into a Tier award at the start of a future stage.  This should make it easier to understand when you are close to an upgrade, and you can adjust how much you invest in weapons accordingly.

[h1]Artwork and Animation Updates[/h1]
Several weapons, icons, ships and other artwork have been slightly improved.

notes.title: Updated to 1.84
notes.content:
[b]A gigantic update to Celtreos![/b]

[h1]Weapon Proficiency (EXP) System![/h1]
You can now improve weapons as you play!  Each time you start a new game though, EXP resets to zero.

Every class of weapon has its own EXP value that accumulates over time.  It does not matter which Series you use: all weapons of the same class will continue to build up EXP for the weapon slot they are in (each weapon array has exactly one weapon of each class).  For example, if you started improving Seeker in one stage and switched to a Series that contained Phaser in another stage, both of these will improve the same weapon slot.

Weapon slots have [i]tiers[/i]. indicated by a bar underneath the new XP display in-game.  Each time you gain a new tier, you receive the associated bonus or weapon update.  Although some effects can apply to several weapon slots, others are entirely unique; keep improving your weapons to see what they can do!

[b]Tiers can only change at the start of a new stage[/b] (when bonuses are awarded), even though EXP accumulates continuously during gameplay.  The EXP scale is also not linear; for example, it is much harder to go from Tier 3 to Tier 4 than it is to go from Tier 1 to Tier 2.

See the help function in-game to learn all about weapon classes, tier bonuses and more.

[h1]New Achievements[/h1]
Several new Achievements have been added to the game, related to the weapon proficiency system.

[h1]Updated Music[/h1]
The “Evacuation” and “Mystery” songs have been refined further.

notes.title: Updated to 1.82
notes.content:
[b]A gigantic update to Celtreos![/b]

[h1]“Hard Difficulty” Setting[/h1]
Enabling this new setting makes the game significantly more challenging!  
[list]
[*] “1UP” power-ups NEVER spawn
[*] Defensive items such as “Shield” are far less likely to spawn
[*] Achievements do not give invincibility (though the Achievement still counts)
[*] Small round bullets are invulnerable and must all be avoided!
[*] Most projectiles are stronger and harder to destroy
[*] Much longer cooldown after using a Charge (“Bomb”, “Lightning”, etc.)
[*] Negative items appear more frequently
[*] Several enemy attack patterns change, and many are also faster
[*] More enemies spawn, and some walls may also change
[/list]

[h1]Updated Music[/h1]
There have been significant soundtrack improvements, updating songs such as “Disposition”, “Assignment”, “Evasion”, “Excursion”, “Confrontation”, “Portension” and “Flow”.

[h1]Artwork, Animation and Effect Updates[/h1]
There have been minor tweaks to a variety of effects, including explosions and shaking.  Some of the UI has improvements, like certain icon artwork and text sizes.  Background contrast has been tweaked in stages like “Alien Ocean”.  The “Predator” weapon has also improved.

The “Colony Evacuation” and “Last Stand” stages now have water lines that cause splash effects when the water is hit by things like bombs, certain bullets and debris.  This opens up a new line of evasion, as you can potentially avoid being hit by flying further down than the water impact point.

[h1]Test Stage Updates[/h1]
Wide-area-effect cooldowns have been removed when “Test…” is used, allowing more rapid experimentation with those abilities.

notes.title: Updated to 1.80
notes.content:
[b]A gigantic update to Celtreos![/b]

It’s been a while since the last update but this one is worth the wait.

[h1]New “Bumper” Defense[/h1]
The “Plasma Series” now has a unique defensive ability, “Bumper”.  This item makes it extremely unlikely that your ship will be destroyed by walls, and it will also push your ship out of the way of such obstacles (be careful though as it provides no protection against enemy attacks).  Note that you can also select this item when defining one of your 5 custom weapon arrays.

[h1]Artwork, Animation and Effect Updates[/h1]
Several stage backgrounds are more detailed, some significantly (such as “Orbital Defense” and “Refinery Raid”).  There are improvements to explosion effects.  Tweaks have been made to artwork and animation in a number of other places.

Also, when certain objects and enemies are impacted by your weapons, they react in more obvious ways (such as gently shaking).

[h1]Gameplay Updates[/h1]
Certain stages have been tweaked for better gameplay, such as “Dark Nebula” (where it is now a bit easier to see through clouds).

A few weapons have been modified to work better, such as beam-based attacks (Beam, Phaser, Ray Burst, Column, etc.), the Predator weapon, and the Magnet Mine weapon.

The in-game weapon display now shows the icons for every weapon currently available to you, not just the name of the active weapon.  In addition, the selected weapon’s icon is slightly larger.  When you have all weapons, these appear in the same ascending order as their key bindings (1-6).

The Achievement display now makes it more obvious that your ship is invincible while this award is on the screen.

[h1]Weapon Mount Items[/h1]
Although you can still set preferred weapon mounts to start the game, there are now in-game items that let you switch to a different kind of mount (currently 5 types).  These options sometimes spawn together at major transition points in a stage but they may also spawn in different ways, even randomly from one play to the next.  The icons for these items are now also shown in the Ship Editor when selecting default mounts.

[h1]Updated Soundtrack with New Song[/h1]
When you browse achievements (via the trophy button on the main options screen), a brand new song is now played!

Several tracks have been enhanced further, including “Disposition”, “Acquisition”, “Evacuation”, “Mystery”, “Portension”, “Fabrication” and “Flow”.

[h1]Sound Effects[/h1]
There are a few new sound effects, including additional explosions.  Some weapons now have new sounds, such as “Tail Whip” and “Weaver”.

[h1]Test Stage Updates[/h1]
There are now more types of targets in the test stage, including some that are much larger (and take more hits to destroy) and more that move.  The new weapon mount items now also periodically spawn here to make it easier to see how other mounts affect your weapons.

notes.title: Updated to 1.79
notes.content:
[b]A big update to Celtreos![/b]

[h1]New Progress Tracking Mode[/h1]
There’s a lot in this game, and you don’t want to miss anything.  Now you can be sure you haven’t, using a new mode that keeps track of the major things you have done!  Use the new “trophy” button on the main options screen to reach this mode.

In the top-left corner of this screen is a basic percentage of overall game progress (this is also displayed on the trophy button itself from the options screen, as a quick reference).

Although Achievements can be triggered any time you play the game, this mode will now keep track of the unique kinds of Achievements that you have ever been awarded.  The conditions for activating them are secret…can you find them all?

There is also a section on general stage-by-stage progress.  Most of these will be gradually awarded through normal gameplay but there are still some interesting ones to unveil!

Finally, there is a 3rd section to cover other aspects of the game.  Initially these are focused on abilities…try to explore all the weapons, defenses and other features of your ship!

If you are having trouble triggering some of these, turn on the “Hints” button to show extra information when selecting each goal, that may help you to understand how to get it.

Try your best to reach 100% but this mode will probably expand over time with even more new secret goals to achieve!!! 

[h1]Gameplay Tweaks[/h1]
As usual, a few minor improvements to artwork, animation and stage design.

[quote][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34873598/61a614864e390b5bdcaa6c50b9efa567821c7ec2.png[/img]
[i]Now you won’t miss a thing, the game keeps track of all your major progress.[/i][/quote]

notes.content:
[b]The next Celtreos patch is live![/b]

[h1]Dynamic Enemy Spawns[/h1]
The game now automatically spawns new enemies when there are few remaining on the screen.  The type of auto-spawn varies by stage, and depends on how well you “clear” an area.  This means you can potentially rack up even more score by quickly defeating enemies, since that will lead to more targets overall.

[h1]General Gameplay Updates[/h1]
Certain stages have improved spawn patterns and layout, such as “Alien Ocean”.  A new plasma-ball projectile has been added, and it is now used by a number of enemies and bosses!

[h1]New Weapon Mount[/h1]
The Ship Editor now has a 5th type of weapon mount, “Crossover”.  This is essentially an X pattern but for single projectiles it travels in an animated way along alternate crossover paths, whereas for 2- and 3-multipliers it will cause each copy of a weapon to follow its own X path.

[h1]Updated Boss Soundtrack[/h1]
A new boss theme “Portension” has been added to the soundtrack, and plays during the “Dark Nebula” and “Refinery Raid” boss fights.

[h1]Artwork and Animation Updates[/h1]
Certain user interface elements have improved.  Minor tweaks have been made to explosions and other effects.  Some enemy ships have updated artwork and animation.

notes.title: Updated to 1.74
notes.content:
[b]A big update to Celtreos![/b]

[h1]Major Game Controller Improvements[/h1]
Controller inputs no longer have [i]any[/i] movement lag, and they have been recalibrated to have more precision and more natural speed curves.  While analog sticks are quite helpful, D-pads have also been tweaked to have two different responses when nudged in a direction vs. being held down.  Note that this is all in [i]addition[/i] to the ways you could already manage your ship speed in the game.

Some user interface elements have been given new controller button mappings so that they are quicker to activate.

Also, the button-mapping help in the main settings screen has been fixed to show correct button labels for PS4 or PS5 controllers.

[h1]Now Available for Apple TV[/h1]
The game has been ported to tvOS so that it can run on an Apple TV!

[h1]New “Zero Score” Negative Item[/h1]
Careful out there, even more hazards…now the red orb with a yellow zero “0” will temporarily [b]prevent any kind of scoring[/b]!

[h1]Updated Artwork[/h1]
Several enemies, bosses, backgrounds and explosion effects in the game look noticeably better!

[h1]Now Requires macOS 10.13 or Later[/h1]
Unfortunately as time moves forward, Apple makes it difficult to continue supporting older Macs so this update requires at least macOS 10.13 “High Sierra” (all previous versions can run on macOS 10.12 “Sierra”).

[quote][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34873598/25fec48ec5adb050acd011f89807238e77166396.png[/img]

notes.title: Updated to 1.73
notes.content:
[b]The next Celtreos patch is live![/b]

[h1]More Stage Content[/h1]
A few stages have been modified significantly, such as “Space Station” and “Refinery Raid”.  There are new sections with entirely different wall layouts, as well as a few minor changes to existing sections.

[h1]Stabilized Opposing-Movement Weapons and Defenses[/h1]
Improvements have been made to things that can be oriented in opposition to ship movement (weapons: “Tail Whip”, “Star Strike”, “Magnetic Mine”, “Sweeper”; defenses: “Barrier”; pods: “Prism”).  These are now stabilized so that they will continue to maintain their most recent orientation if your ship does not move a significant amount, such as when you are staying in one place.  This should make these much easier to control, more intuitive and ultimately more useful.

[h1]New 2500-Point Score Bonus[/h1]
In addition to the existing 500-point and 10000-point bonus items, now there is a 2500-point middle tier.  This appears throughout various stages of the game in some areas that may be tricky to reach, and it can also appear as part of fragment bonuses.

The “Devastator Series” is continuing to expand, this time with a new default weapon option, “Ring”.  This weapon actually looks similar to the original look of “Blaster”, and “Blaster” now has a new appearance!

notes.title: Nominate “Celtreos” for the “Labor of Love” Award!
notes.content:
[h1]“Celtreos” is a “Labor of Love”![/h1]
This game was [b]first released in 2017[/b] but has been [b]updated over 65 times[/b] (including late 2021), on average [i]once a month[/i], making [b]huge additions[/b] such as:
[list]
[*] New stages
[*] Improved soundtrack and brand new songs!
[*] Two-player mode
[*] Many, many new weapons over time, and the ability to customize weapon arrays
[*] New ships, and an entirely new ship-customization mode
[*] New power-ups and other game items
[*] New enemies, and even a 2nd end-game boss!
[*] New gameplay features such as Achievements, Fragments and rotating stages
[*] New controls such as ship slow-down and changing default speed
[*] Improved game artwork continuously (making more detailed backgrounds for instance)
[*] Support for the latest operating systems, computer hardware and game controllers!
[*] Redesign to support wider-screen format
[*] Upgrading effects and voice to support positional sound
[*] Continuous improvements to performance and other low-level aspects of the code
[*] Localization of the in-game UI to French
[/list]

[h1]Remastered and Updated Soundtrack[/h1]
Several songs have been tweaked, including: “Disposition”, “Navigation”, “Obliteration”, “Assignment”, “Acquisition”, “Confrontation”, “Flow” and “Excursion”.  Also, songs have been re-exported with higher-quality source instruments for even better sound!

There are two new “smoke” colors and two new “stream” colors!  There are now a total of 10 options for ship exhaust effects.

notes.title: Updated to 1.60
notes.content:
[b]A big update to Celtreos![/b]

[h1]New Ship Editor[/h1]
The ship-editing interface is now an entirely separate screen that has more options than before, and more-detailed ship artwork, too!

Select from [b]4 weapon mounts[/b], including: default (original), high/low, front/back, and circular!  These create awesome new attacks and drastically change the behavior of certain weapons.  They also affect the “×2” and “×3” firing patterns!

[h1]New Test Stage[/h1]
A [b]test stage[/b] can now be launched directly from the new ship editor, to try out your current arrangement.  This lets you loose in a simulation full of power-ups and targets to shoot at!

[h1]New Songs[/h1]
The new ship editor has distinct background music.  In addition, a new [b]alternate stage-clear song[/b] “Perfection” is played when you achieve the highest possible shooting [i]and[/i] time bonuses (50,000 points each).

[h1]Gameplay Improvements[/h1]
Bonuses have been made more accurate.  The shooting bonus now correctly takes into account the number of enemies that actually spawn (making high bonuses possible in later stages that have few enemies, as long as you take out most of them).  The time bonus has also been tweaked to have more realistic target times for each stage.

The hit-boxes of each ship model have been tweaked further to make them tighter.  This will make the differences between each of the 7 ships more noticeable.
